title: Endogenous Greedy Expansions: Exactness, Boundary Geometry, and Recovery of Analytic Dynamics
content: We study a greedy expansion in which the centre being represented generates its own two-sided sequence of iterated weights. For convex analytic interval maps we give a complete criterion for global exactness, involving the attracting multiplier, a central orbit sum, and an independent repelling-endpoint obstruction. Outside the convex class, strict endpoint conditions reduce exactness to finitely many real inequalities. For \( 0\lt F'(0)\lt 1/2 \), the actual set of exact centres has Hausdorff dimension \( \log 2/|\log F'(0)| \); at a superattracting endpoint it has dimension zero and contains a Cantor set. With two hyperbolic endpoints, the first-selection boundaries exhibit a periodic endpoint modulation. We construct distinct analytic systems with the same entire first-boundary sequence but different exactness phases. By contrast, three prescribed rows of second-selection thresholds determine every analytic system with a hyperbolic attracting endpoint; the opposite endpoint may be hyperbolic or parabolic. A nonconstant endpoint connection, or a superattracting endpoint, makes one row sufficient. On fixed complex analytic priors, the optimal recovery error \( \Omega(\delta) \) satisfies \( -\log\Omega(\delta)\asymp\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)} \) in the hyperbolic case and \( -\log\Omega(\delta)\asymp\log\log(1/\delta) \) for fixed superattracting degree. The corresponding deterministic query bounds identify the joint dependence on noise and the number of scalar measurements. All lower bounds are realized by actual analytic conjugacies, and an exponential query obstruction persists when both threshold indices are chosen adaptively without restriction.
